preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `clean_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Restore reliable, event-causal combat by making mouse and gamepad fire use one authoritative edge path, binding directional player-damage presentation to the shipped player, and making checkpoint restoration an atomic enemy-state transaction while preserving the accepted map, viewmodels, 18-enemy roster, mission order, and clean boot.

diagnosis.root_cause: Three integration defects prevent trustworthy combat replay. Fire currently mixes raw `_input` delivery, per-frame polling, and handoff-time physical-level latching, so a short gamepad trigger edge can be swallowed or interpreted differently depending on frame stepping. The existing damage-feedback scene is not instantiated in `main.tscn` and expects an `FPSHealth` source, while the shipped `PrototypePlayer` exposes a different damage signal that discards direction/source metadata; authoritative health loss therefore has no bound directional presentation listener. Checkpoint restoration writes only a subset of each live enemy's snapshot and immediately resumes processing, leaving base-combat perception memory, targets, attack timing, navigation intent, and reservations alive across the restore. The repeated Alpha progression finding is an evidence-access blocker, not justification for another route-transform tuning pass: prior evidence also records a collision-clear route, so this iteration should repair combat state and use fresh ordinary-input traversal only for retest access.

stop_conditions: Stop and report the exact node, collision contact, and player transform if a fresh ordinary-input run cannot reach Alpha; do not perform another speculative spawn, objective, map, collision, or navigation transform-tuning pass in this iteration.
Stop if either repair would require replacing or surgically modifying the preserved authored environment, AK-74M hands/viewmodel, enemy presentation package, or stable 3/5/10 roster.
Stop if a proposed presentation listener can create damage, health, ammo, score, objective, or checkpoint truth; all feedback must remain an idempotent observer of authoritative event IDs.
Stop and preserve the prior candidate if clean boot regresses, scripts fail to parse, resource paths fail to load, or runtime logs contain new errors attributable to these edits.
Stop after the focused developer retest is enabled; GameLoop Runtime and QA Tester own continuous-frame recapture, formal verdicts, issue closure, and phase closure.

strategy.rationale: Use a materially different root-cause strategy after three no-progress rounds: replace the competing fire latches with one queued action-edge authority; repair the dead damage-feedback binding rather than adding an unrelated overlay; and restore existing enemy instances through an explicit suspend/restore/reacquire epoch rather than tuning transforms or reaction delays. This directly addresses causality and lifecycle boundaries while retaining the preserved authored map, weapon rigs, and proven AI behavior.

code: Parse all edited GDScript and load all edited scenes/resources without warnings promoted to errors; run the preserved clean-boot check.

Inspect the final signal graph to confirm PrototypePlayer remains the sole player-health authority, WeaponController remains the sole player-shot/ammo authority, and feedback nodes only observe immutable events.
Verify the enemy restore API distinguishes durable checkpoint fields from volatile combat state and that no partial restore path can resume physics or attack authorization early.
runtime: Developer focused self-check: fresh-deploy separately with mouse and gamepad, exercising short press, AUTO hold/release, pause/resume, and checkpoint restore. Compare input edge ID, source, shot ID, magazine before/after, commit count, and release/cancellation reason.

GameLoop Runtime/Tester recapture: use one ordinary-input traversal along the live collision-backed route into Alpha without state injection. If traversal fails, capture the blocking collider/node and stop instead of retuning transforms.

GameLoop Runtime/Tester recapture: record one enemy shot from aim telegraph through recovery and align actor/shot ID, enemy ammo, muzzle/tracer or impact result, player damage event, health change, directional feedback state, and camera response. Repeat a miss/blocked or near-miss case and require no fabricated health loss.

GameLoop Runtime/Tester recapture: engage Alpha, commit a checkpoint, allow actors to change position/ammo/target state, die, and restart. Compare all three actors immediately before death, during the suspended restore epoch, before control returns, and through fresh perception/aim/first legal shot. Repeat once for determinism and confirm countdown time is not increased.
visual: At 1280×720, capture adjacent frames for damage onset, peak, and decay from the shipped first-person camera. The red edge/arc must indicate source direction, scale with severity, preserve enemy/world visibility, and leave the reticle, health, ammo, countdown, and objective readable.

Capture matched mouse and gamepad fire peak/recovery frames and confirm the accepted AK-74M hands/viewmodel, muzzle feedback, recoil, ammo HUD, and world result remain synchronized to their unique shot IDs.

Capture Alpha immediately after checkpoint restore and after fresh reacquisition. The first frame must show restored, non-firing actors with no stale muzzle/tracer event; later fire must follow a visible aim telegraph and retain separation, grounded presentation, and the accepted environment composition.

done_when: From the same fresh AK-74M magazine state, a short ordinary real-time mouse-left press and a short ordinary real-time gamepad right-trigger press each commit exactly one unique input edge and one unique authoritative shot immediately, decrement the magazine once, preserve the correct source label, and produce the same ballistic/result receipt shape.

The stepped gamepad path and ordinary real-time path have identical exactly-once press/release semantics; AUTO hold follows the configured rate, release stops scheduling immediately, and raw input plus polling cannot duplicate a shot.

Pause, death, checkpoint restore, loadout/page handoff, and gameplay re-enable cancel or re-arm fire deterministically: a trigger held across the boundary cannot fire until a genuine release followed by a new press.

The shipped player emits one immutable damage payload containing event/shot ID, source position, amount/severity, and health after damage. A bound feedback instance observes it within two rendered frames and displays a directional red edge/arc, bounded severity-scaled camera response, and synchronized health change without obscuring the map, reticle, or objective HUD.

Blocked, missed, duplicated, paused, restored, and terminal-state events cannot fabricate or replay damage feedback. Active damage tweens settle or cancel on restore/death, and the feedback state exposes the observed event ID, direction, severity, alpha/lifetime, and camera-response state for focused runtime inspection.

The premium tactical presentation remains sparse and world-readable in the supplied visual direction: graphite/cyan HUD stays legible while red is reserved for transient enemy damage, with no opaque full-screen card or persistent pure-red wash.
tasks.instructions: Refactor the weapon input boundary around a single queued press/release edge authority shared by mouse and mapped analog fire. Do not fix the gamepad symptom by lowering deadzones, lengthening injected input, or layering another independent poll; retain InputMap support but ensure one physical transition is consumed once after gameplay eligibility is known. Extend the shipped PrototypePlayer damage event without creating a second health authority, instantiate and adapt the existing FPSPlayerDamageFeedback scene in the shipped main composition, and bind it to authoritative damage metadata. Add directional and severity-aware transient presentation plus a small restrained camera impulse, with idempotence and cancellation keyed by the damage event ID. Keep all existing weapon/viewmodel, ammo, ballistics, HUD, and controlled-target behavior intact.
tasks.title: Unify authoritative fire input and bind complete player-damage feedback

done_when: Checkpoint restore suspends enemy simulation and attack authorization before any player, weapon, mission, or roster state is mutated, and resumes only after the complete versioned snapshot has been applied.

Every restored actor retains its stable ID, region, role, route slot, alive/health state, checkpoint transform, ammunition, activation state, and presentation binding, while stale target references, visibility/last-seen memory, attack/reload timers, pending shot state, navigation destination/velocity, avoidance/reservation state, cleanup timers, and transient presentation state are explicitly re-?

No restored enemy can fire on the first resumed frame or reuse a pre-death shot/target. A new shot is legal only after fresh perception/line-of-sight acquisition and the normal deterministic aim telegraph window.

Repeating restore from the same checkpoint produces the same actor snapshot before control returns, does not grant countdown time, does not duplicate checkpoint commits or enemy events, and does not change the accepted 3 Alpha, 5 Bravo, and 10 Charlie identities.

After restoration, the previously verified search, locomotion, acquisition, aim, fire, ammo consumption, reload, reposition, separation, hit, and death behavior remains available; the repair does not globally disable AI, reduce the roster, teleport actors, or reset mission difficulty.

The roster/runtime state exposes a restore epoch and per-actor restored/quiescent/readiness fields sufficient to align the snapshot, resume boundary, fresh perception, aim window, and first legal post-restore shot without relying on a UI dictionary alone.
tasks.instructions: Implement an atomic restore epoch across MissionController, EnemyRoster, and the existing enemy instances. Freeze AI/attack/navigation first, restore authoritative durable fields, clear all volatile base-combat state through an explicit reset method, rebind presentation and collision/avoidance consistently, then resume with target acquisition gated behind a fresh perception and aim window. Preserve monotonic event/shot IDs where replay ambiguity would otherwise occur, and record one restore transaction receipt rather than emitting actor activity during the partial state. Do not alter map placement, enemy roster slots, difficulty tuning, or route geometry to mask the defect.
tasks.title: Make enemy checkpoint restoration atomic and perception-safe
